question: How does the 2025 VA pharmacotherapy summary say to start and titrate basal insulin, and what if hypoglycemia occurs?
answer: The 2025 VA T2DM pharmacotherapy summary says to start **basal insulin** (NPH, glargine, or degludec) as **one injection daily at bedtime**. Initial dose: **10 units once daily** or **0.1–0.2 units/kg once daily**. Set an individualized **FPG target range**, then titrate using SMBG FPG: **increase 10–15% weekly** or **increase by 2 units every 3 days**. If the patient has **hypoglycemia**, **decrease the insulin dose by 10–20%**. It also notes glargine is preferred initially over NPH due to less hypoglycemia.

va_pbm_t2dm_pharmacotherapy_2025 (VA, advisory, 2025-04)
Pharmacotherapy for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) 2025: A VA Clinician's Summary (IB 10-1775) > Initiating insulin > Prandial (mealtime) insulin1,2
[p 8]
Prandial (mealtime) insulin 1,2
Prandial insulins include aspart, glulisine, lispro, and regular.
■ Consider GLP-1 RA before adding prandial insulin if inadequate glycemic control on basal insulin and one or more oral agents. 47
■ Add prandial insulin when coverage is needed for meals. Consider when HbA1c continues to be above goal, basal insulin dose is > 0.5 units/kg, or glucose readings are elevated after meals.
■ Rapid acting insulins like aspart, glulisine, and lispro should be administered 0-15 minutes before meals and are preferred to insulin regular due to easier administration.
■ Insulin regular should be administered 30 minutes before meals. The longer time of onset and duration may increase hypoglycemia risk. 48
[p 9]
Figure 6. Using prandial insulin
[Figure, flowchart] untitled in the image; see the section heading (PDF page 9). Machine-generated visual interpretation; status: machine-interpreted from the page image by a vision model; structure and OCR cross-check passed.
Box n1 (start): Starting prandial insulin • Start with one dose before the largest meal of the day. • Use in addition to basal insulin. • Begin with 4 units or 10% of basal dose. • Discontinue sulfonylurea, meglitinides, and DPP-4 I. -> if Home glucose* or HbA1c over target range: box n2
Box n2 (action): Titrating prandial insulin • Increase dose by 1 to 2 units or 10 to 15% twice weekly • If having hypoglycemia, determine the cause (e.g., missed meal, exercise). - If no clear reason, lower dose by 10 to 20% -> if HbA1c over target range: box n3
Box n3 (action): Adding prandial doses • Start with adding a second prandial dose and follow titration schedule • Recheck HbA1c in 3 months • If HbA1c still elevated, adjust regimen based on glucose patterns; consider adding a third prandial insulin dose
Decision path: n1 -> [Home glucose* or HbA1c over target range] n2 -> [HbA1c over target range] n3
Unreadable or ambiguous (not interpreted): Footnote text for the asterisk on 'Home glucose*' is not visible in the crop
■ Insulin aspart protamine/insulin aspart 70/30 (Novolog 70/30) or insulin 70/30 NPH/REG (Novolin 70/30) - Note these are look-alike, sound-alike drugs.
■ Need to have regular meal routines and not skip meals.
■ Novolog 70/30 is preferred since it is administered 0-15 minutes before mealtime, while Novolin 70/30 is administered 30 minutes before eating.
